description: statemodify is a Python package for editing inputs to the StateMod water-allocation model. It helps users apply changes to demands, supplies or operating assumptions in a repeatable scenario workflow and prepare the resulting model files. The JOSS paper discusses drought vulnerability in Colorado River basins, but the software can operate on other StateMod configurations supplied by a user. Its geographic coverage and simulation period are therefore inherited from those files, not built into the package. The public repository and README describe installation and use under BSD-2-Clause. The tool can support comparisons of drought, water-rights or demand scenarios for irrigation, drinking-water and reservoir systems. A caveat is that modifying input files does not independently test whether the StateMod baseline or water-rights rules are accurate. Scenario results also depend on the separate StateMod engine. No catalogue or first-review record matched this named helper package. The JOSS summary, own metadata and documentation were read without running a basin scenario.
